subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & data residency (EU/APAC)
participants_external: anna.svensson@scandibank.se (Anna Svensson, Head of Cloud Platform)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Svensson <anna.svensson@scandibank.se>
Cc: Michael Bengtsson <michael.bengtsson@scandibank.se>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:03:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & data residency (EU/APAC)

Hi Anna — thanks again for the intro call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the deployment options given ScandiBank's residency requirements.

Recap of requirements I heard:
- Primary production data (customer PII and transaction metadata) must remain in EU (Sweden/EU)
- Some APAC traffic needs to be served with low latency and ideally data processed in-region for regulatory reasons
- A subset of workloads (risk scoring, transaction forensics) may require tighter controls and potentially an on-prem or VPC-only deployment

Options we discussed (short):
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted, EU region): fastest to get started; we can restrict data routing to our EU region + SOC2 controls. Good for lower-sensitivity workloads and MVPs.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in a customer-dedicated tenant in EU — predictable throughput, stronger isolation, can offer stricter network controls (private peering).
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed private control plane and optional on-prem package — recommended for regulated workloads needing full network/isolation and customer KMS/HSM.

Questions / confirmations we need from you to prioritize next steps:
- Which production workloads MUST be strictly EU-only (and require on-prem/VPC) vs which can live in Hosted EU?
- APAC: do you need a separate APAC instance or is cross-region routing acceptable if data is kept in EU (i.e., frontend in APAC, processing in EU)?
- Any specific compliance artifacts beyond SOC2 (e.g., data flow diagrams, subprocessors list, encryption-at-rest key custody requirements)?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send our region availability matrix and SOC2 summary (attached) so you can share with Security/Procurement
- If it looks good, I’ll loop in Solutions Eng for a technical deep-dive next week to validate network/KMS options and latency tests
- We can then produce a tailored SOW and a ballpark pricing for Dedicated/Private options

If you can reply with the bullet answers to the three questions above, I’ll get the SE scheduled. Available times for a 60m session next week: Tue 11/17 09:00-11:30 CET or Wed 11/18 13:00-16:00 CET.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. Answers below:

- Strict EU-only (production): core customer PII ingestion and transaction history must remain processed and stored in EU. These will need to be considered for Dedicated or Private depending on network/KMS needs.
- APAC: We have a fintech vertical in APAC that needs low latency; our preference is local processing in APAC for that vertical but we can consider routing if latency is within 120ms.
- Compliance artifacts: please include SOC2, list of subprocessors, data flow diagram, and an encryption/KMS summary including whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys or HSM integrations.

Procurement flagged that they will need a sample SOW and any standard redlines early in the process. Michael from SecOps will take the technical lead; cc'd.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment mode & data residency (EU/APAC)

Anna — great, thanks for the clarity. I’ve attached a short region availability matrix and our SOC2 summary. Quick answers inline to your bullets: 

- EU-only production: We support Hosted in EU regions (data residency limited to EU) and Dedicated in EU (reserved capacity with stronger isolation). For workloads that need full customer control over networking/KMS and on-prem hardware, Private (VPC or on-prem package) is available — that is our recommended path for the most sensitive workloads.
- APAC low-latency: We can deploy Dedicated/Private nodes in APAC regions; for Hosted customers, we currently offer a hosted APAC region but for strict residency and latency SLAs Dedicated or Private is preferred. Cross-region routing is possible, but for regulated workloads where processing locality matters we recommend separate region deployments.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSM via our Private offering).

Attachments: Redwood-Region-Matrix-20261115.pdf (region availability and recommended deployment modes), SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (summary), SOW-sample-Redwood-20261115.pdf (sample SOW).

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Loop in Solutions Engs for the technical deep-dive — Rafael will lead the session to validate network diagrams, peering options, and KMS flows.
2) Prepare a ballpark price comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for core EU production workloads.
3) Provide standard contract template / sample SOW for procurement to review.

Rafael — can you own the SE session? We’re looking at Tue 11/17 09:00-10:00 CET (Anna preferred slot).

Thanks — Marissa
